document_title: CO2 Baseline Database for the Indian Power Sector User Guide
text_content: The weighted average emission factor for the Indian national electricity grid (including renewable energy sources) stands at 0.716 tCO2/MWh for the evaluated reporting period. Operating Margin (OM) is established at 0.892 tCO2/MWh, while Build Margin (BM) is calculated at 0.540 tCO2/MWh. State-level emission variations arise from regional generation mixes but CEA officially publishes national and regional grid values.

document_title: UK Government GHG Conversion Factors for Company Reporting 2026
text_content: Stationary combustion conversion factors for standard industrial fuels: 100% mineral diesel accounts for 2.684 kgCO2e per litre; standard commercial natural gas yields 2.023 kgCO2e per standard cubic metre (Gross CV basis); and LPG produces 2.939 kgCO2e per kilogram. All factors include CO2, CH4, and N2O expressed in CO2 equivalent using IPCC AR5 Global Warming Potentials.

document_title: BEE Energy & Resource Mapping in 55 Indian MSME Clusters
section: Thermal & Electrical Specific Energy Consumption Benchmarks
text_content: In the Morbi Ceramics cluster, vitrified and wall tile manufacturing exhibits an official reported thermal SEC range between 4.80 and 9.20 GJ per tonne of finished product, with a median of 6.40 GJ/t. Electrical SEC ranges between 120 and 260 kWh/t, with a median of 180 kWh/t. Roller kilns represent over 78% of total thermal energy consumption, making flue gas waste heat recovery the single highest impact intervention.

document_title: Guidance for Importers on the Definitive Regime of the EU CBAM
section: Covered Goods in Iron, Steel and Aluminium
text_content: Under the definitive regime beginning 2026, Indian exporters of covered iron, steel, and aluminium goods into the European Union must report both direct (Scope 1) and indirect (Scope 2) embedded emissions. If primary producer EPDs are absent, European Commission default benchmarks apply (e.g. 2.19 tCO2e/t for HRC, 1.98 tCO2e/t for rebar). PRANGARA outputs for CBAM liability are classified as INDICATIVE CBAM EXPOSURE.

document_title: Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS) Framework & Sector Guidelines
section: Obligated Entity Thresholds and Third-Party Verification
text_content: Under the Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (CCTS), industrial plants with an annual energy consumption exceeding sector thresholds (e.g., 30,000 toe/year for Iron & Steel, 10,000 toe/year for Cement) are notified as Obligated Entities. Obligated entities must reduce specific GHG emission intensity against baseline targets or purchase Carbon Credit Certificates (CCCs). Verification must be performed by BEE-accredited Validation & Verification Bodies (VVBs).

document_title: SEBI Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR) Core Framework
section: Value Chain ESG Disclosures & Scope 3 Supplier Assurance
text_content: Under the SEBI BRSR Core mandate, India’s top 1000 listed entities must disclose Scope 1, Scope 2, and key Scope 3 greenhouse gas emissions, energy intensity per rupee of turnover, and water consumption across their value chain partners (suppliers and vendors accounting for 75% of purchases by value). MSME vendors in the value chain must provide auditable activity records or undergo reasonable assurance by independent certified assurance providers.

document_title: CPCB Guidelines for Consent to Establish (CTE) and Consent to Operate (CTO)
section: Industrial Siting, Air & Water Pollution Consent Standards
text_content: All industrial facilities classified under Red, Orange, or Green categories must obtain Consent to Establish (CTE) before construction and Consent to Operate (CTO) before commercial production under Section 25 of the Water Act 1974 and Section 21 of the Air Act 1981. Periodic renewal requires submission of annual Environmental Statements (Form V), continuous emission monitoring system (CEMS) telemetry, and verification of zero liquid discharge (ZLD) or compliant effluent discharge parameters.

document_title: Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules
section: Co-Processing, Form 10 Manifests and Recycling Authorization
text_content: Hazardous wastes such as chemical sludge, ETP cake, and spent solvents must be transported under Form 10 yellow manifests to authorized TSDF facilities or licensed co-processing units (e.g. cement kilns for energy and material recovery). Senders, transporters, and receivers must record consignments on the CPCB National Hazardous Waste Tracking Portal, with strict prohibitions on unauthorized landfill disposal.

document_title: MoEFCC Notification on Mandatory 100% Fly Ash Utilisation
page: Gazette of India Extraordinary Part II
section: Mandatory Utilization for Thermal Plants and Building Material Makers
text_content: All coal or lignite-based thermal power plants must achieve 100% utilization of fly ash and bottom ash within a designated compliance cycle. Construction agencies within a 300-kilometer radius are statutorily mandated to use only fly ash bricks, blocks, or tiles for paving and masonry. Unutilized fly ash attracts environmental compensation penalties of ₹1,000 per tonne collected by the Central Pollution Control Board.

document_title: IS 12615 / IEC 60034-30-1: Energy Efficient Induction Motors
section: Efficiency Classes (IE1, IE2, IE3, IE4) and Star Labelling Standards
text_content: Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) standard IS 12615 mandates energy performance standards for three-phase squirrel cage induction motors. Line-operated motors are categorised into Standard Efficiency (IE1), High Efficiency (IE2), Premium Efficiency (IE3), and Super Premium Efficiency (IE4). Under BEE regulations, replacement of sub-IE2 motors with IE3 or IE4 units delivers 3% to 8% direct electrical energy savings with typical industrial payback periods under 18 months.

document_title: GLEC Framework Logistics Emission Guidance for India
section: Road Freight Carbon Factors, Empty Backhauls and Multi-Tenant Pooling
text_content: Smart Freight Centre (SFC) India establishes baseline freight emission intensity: rigid 16-tonne diesel trucks emit 0.089 kgCO2e/t-km at 75% load factor, while 28-tonne articulated trailers emit 0.062 kgCO2e/t-km. Running an unladen return journey increases total trip carbon intensity by 45%. Implementing multi-tenant truck pooling and digital circular backhauls directly offsets Scope 3 Category 4 transportation footprints.

document_title: GHG Protocol Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard
section: Scope 1 Direct, Scope 2 Indirect, and Scope 3 Value Chain Rules
text_content: The GHG Protocol defines corporate accounting boundaries under two distinct approaches: Equity Share and Financial/Operational Control. Under Operational Control, an entity accounts for 100% of emissions from operations over which it has the full authority to introduce and implement operating policies. Direct fossil combustion within plant boundaries is classified as Scope 1; imported grid electricity and steam as Scope 2; and third-party freight and raw material supply chain as Scope 3.
